title: Encoding of Sound Source Elevation in Human Cortex
description: This EEG dataset contains recordings from two experiments in which participants listened to noise bursts presented from loudspeakers at different elevations in a hemi-anechoic chamber. Experiment 1 was a deviant detection task with adapter and probe sounds, and Experiment 2 was a one-back localization task. Participants first completed a behavioral test of their ability to localize elevated sound sources. The dataset supports research on how sound source elevation is encoded in human auditory cortex.
methods_description: Pink noise bursts were presented from loudspeakers at several elevations at 10° azimuth to the listener's right. Localization tests preceded each experiment. Experiment 1 (sub-001 to sub-023) used a long adapter noise followed by a short probe burst from another loudspeaker, with deviant trials requiring a button press. Experiment 2 (sub-100 to sub-129) used long white noise over open headphones followed by a noise burst from a loudspeaker. About 5% of trials were targets, followed by a beep prompting the subject to localize the sound.
